data.jobspec:
#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -N 1
#   -n 1
#   --mem=16G
#   -o log/process_join_annotate_counts.out
#   -e log/process_join_annotate_counts.err
#   --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --output=log/process_join_annotate_counts.out
#flux: --error=log/process_join_annotate_counts.err

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=16G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic job emails.

eval "$(spack load --sh miniconda3)"
source activate active-learning

python3 src/process_and_join_counts.py
python3 src/annotate_data.py

reasons: The original Slurm job requested 16G of memory (`--mem=16G`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.
